value.rationale: Stable frozen permutation is a meaningful baseline in random-reshuffling optimization, and its failure to guarantee mean-square safety under fresh random permutations is important and sharply quantified here by a universal all-initial-state rational witness. The exact disconnected rate regions explain a genuine parameter-selection issue distinct from simple single-curvature textbook tuning. Not a claim about general nonlinear convergence.
